timing.note: 6183 minutes across 429 experiments. The prior milestone (2026.04.30) logged 6273 minutes across 445 experiments. The apparent reduction in totals reflects re-scoping of the cumulative count — 16 experiments from the prior milestone's running tally were reclassified as blocked/invalid and excluded from the completed count. The 14 min/exp mean is stable and confirms no regression in per-experiment execution pace. The 103-hour wall clock span for 429 experiments represents approximately 18 calendar days of continuous conductor activity at current GPU throughput.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 219: Live GSM8K semantic benchmark on Qwen3.5-0.8B and Gemma
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sequential single-GPU inference with no DualGPURunner, no model pre-warm, and cold-start CUDA initialization absorbed into experiment wall time. Z3 constraint calls were sequential with no per-call timeout, causing constraint evaluation to serialize across all 200 questions. At 14 min average, this experiment took 8.4x the fleet mean — the entire excess came from infrastructure gaps that existed at Exp 219 and have since been addressed in ExperimentTemplate.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 308: JEPA fast-path gate integration (checkpoint — tests failing)
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Failure recovery triggered full 6500-test suite reruns on each fix iteration instead of targeted module-level reruns. Each full suite run took approximately 8 minutes; the fix required 3-4 iterations, wasting 24-32 minutes on tests entirely unrelated to the failing module. Root cause: no guidance in conductor or ExperimentTemplate to prefer targeted reruns during active debugging.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 184: 3B model verification — does verify-repair help large models
slowest_experiments.root_cause: 3B model loaded on single GPU without pre-warm; lazy CUDA initialization stall (~30-45 seconds) was absorbed into timing rather than isolated before the timed inference window. No batching — questions sent one at a time, serializing both GPU scheduling latency and response parsing overhead. GPU 1 sat idle throughout.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 221: Live prompt-side constraint benchmark on typed IR tasks
slowest_experiments.root_cause: Sequential inference with per-question Z3 calls and no per-call timeout. One malformed constraint caused Z3 to spin for over 10 minutes before the outer experiment loop timed out. A 30-second per-call subprocess timeout would have contained the damage to a single question instead of stalling the entire benchmark.

slowest_experiments.description: Exp 155: Retrain JEPA violation predictor v2 with multi-domain data
slowest_experiments.root_cause: CPU training of the full JEPA model on a multi-domain dataset without checkpoint-resume. A mid-run crash required a full restart from epoch 0, costing approximately 40 minutes. ExperimentTemplate.checkpoint_save() now exists and is documented but was not available at Exp 155's time. Modern experiments that omit checkpoint_save() in training loops repeat this failure mode.

gpu_utilization.finding_gpu_0: GPU 0 is ACTIVELY utilized — 88% compute utilization, 64% VRAM, 82C. This represents the first milestone retro captured with a live inference process in-flight. The high temperature (82C) is within safe operating range for RTX 3090 (TJmax 93C) but is the highest recorded across all milestone retros. Sustained 88% utilization over 144+ minutes confirms the process is doing real inference work. The slight utilization drop from the prior snapshot (91% → 88%) at identical VRAM may indicate GPU thermal headroom management as the chip approaches 82-83C.
gpu_utilization.finding_gpu_1: GPU 1 has 1786MB allocated by the SAME process (PID 3509070) but shows 0% utilization. This is the canonical zombie pattern: the process opened both GPUs (likely for DualGPURunner-style setup) but is only actively computing on GPU 0. GPU 1's 1786MB is held idle for the duration of the experiment. The GPU 1 temperature (47C) versus GPU 0 (82C) — a 35-degree delta — confirms GPU 1 is doing zero compute work while GPU 0 carries the full inference load.
gpu_utilization.finding_thermal: GPU 0 at 82C after 144 minutes of sustained 88% utilization. The RTX 3090 throttle threshold is approximately 83-85C. With only 1-3C of headroom, throughput reduction from thermal throttling is plausible if observed in experiment output. GPU 1 has cooled from 51C (prior snapshot) to 47C while GPU 0 held steady at 82C — confirming GPU 1 is completely thermally idle. Physical cooling inspection (fans, heatsink paste, chassis airflow) is recommended before the next extended live session.
gpu_utilization.finding_process_runtime: PID 3509070 has now run 144.65 minutes wall time. A 45-minute hard timeout (RETRO-003) would have terminated this process at the 45-minute mark — freeing GPU 1's 1786MB and the GPU 0 slot for the next experiment 99 minutes ago. The process has now consumed 3.2x the proposed timeout budget with GPU 1 producing zero inference output for its entire duration.

gpu_utilization.retro_022_status: RETRO-022 partially mitigated: Exp 413 implemented apply_env_autofix() which patches the environment at process start and produced honest_verdict=auto_fix_applied. Exps 419 now gate on Exp 413 verdict in approved set. However, the underlying conductor subprocess.run() env inheritance bug is still not fixed at the conductor level — apply_env_autofix() is a workaround executed inside the experiment script, not a systemic fix. The 5-line conductor fix (explicit env={..., 'CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE': '1'}) remains unimplemented.

zombie_processes.classification: partial_zombie — process is active on GPU 0 (88% util) but holds GPU 1 memory at 0% utilization. The process has run 144.65 minutes. A 45-minute hard timeout (RETRO-003) would have freed this slot 99 minutes ago. This is not a true zombie (process is alive and productive on GPU 0) but represents 144+ GPU-minutes of wasted VRAM on the second RTX 3090 and a blocked experiment queue.
zombie_processes.recommendation: Diagnose whether PID 3509070 is a single-model or dual-model experiment. If single-model: GPU 1 should never have been allocated. If dual-model: GPU 1 model load failed silently — add a DualGPURunner health check asserting GPU 1 utilization > 0% within 60 seconds of model load. In either case: implement RETRO-003 conductor hard timeout immediately.
zombie_processes.prior_milestone_comparison: Prior milestone (2026.04.30): both GPUs idle at 2MB each (clean). Current milestone: GPU 0 fully active at 15736MB, GPU 1 partially allocated at 1796MB with 0% utilization. Improvement: we now have a live inference process (RETRO-022 partial fix via Exp 413). Regression: GPU 1 VRAM is held but unused for 144+ minutes — a new inefficiency not seen in prior retros.

bottlenecks_identified: CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE env propagation bug (RETRO-022, workaround applied but root cause unresolved): Exp 413 implemented apply_env_autofix() as a per-experiment workaround, producing honest_verdict=auto_fix_applied. This allowed Exp 419 to pass Gate 0 and reach live GPU inference. However, the conductor subprocess.run() env inheritance bug remains unpatched — each new experiment script must explicitly call apply_env_autofix() before any CUDA import, or it will fail at preflight. The systemic fix (5-line change in conductor) has been deferred for 8+ consecutive milestones.

GPU 1 allocated but idle during active inference (PID 3509070, 144+ minutes): The live process holds 1786MB on GPU 1 at 0% utilization while GPU 0 runs at 88% compute. In the 144-minute experiment window, this represents approximately 144 GPU-minutes of wasted capacity on the second RTX 3090. Root cause is likely a DualGPURunner initialization that allocates both GPUs for device reservation but fails to schedule work on GPU 1 — possibly because the second model variant did not load or the inference queue was not partitioned.

No per-experiment hard timeout in conductor (RETRO-003, carried 17+ milestones): Exp 219 ran 117 minutes; PID 3509070 has now run 144+ minutes. A 45-minute hard cap per experiment would have killed this process 99 minutes ago, freed GPU 1, and allowed at least 2-3 additional experiments to run in the reclaimed time. This is the longest-standing unimplemented infrastructure item in the project.

GPU 0 at 82C under sustained load — approaching throttle threshold: RTX 3090 TJmax is 93C; thermal throttle begins at approximately 83-85C. With 144 minutes at 88% utilization, the GPU has been operating within the danger band for over 2 hours. The utilization drop from 91% (prior snapshot) to 88% (current snapshot) at identical VRAM may already reflect early thermal management. Physical cooling inspection is required before the next extended live session.

Full test suite reruns on targeted failures (Exp 308 pattern): the 14 min/exp mean includes experiments where failure recovery triggered full 6500-test suite reruns multiple times. Targeted reruns (pytest on the failing module only) would cut debugging time by 70% on these cases.

Slow experiment outliers inflate mean and mask throughput improvements: the top 5 slowest experiments (avg 92 min) represent 460 out of 6183 total minutes — 7.4% of all wall time for 1.2% of experiments. Each outlier represents an infrastructure gap (no pre-warm, no timeout, no batching, no checkpoint-resume) that ExperimentTemplate now prevents for new experiments.

Doc reconciliation as a serial post-experiment cost: each experiment ends with 4-6 sequential read-edit-write passes across changelog.md, status.md, conductor-log.md, metrics.md, traceability.md, and spec.md. For fast-path experiments (14 min mean), the doc pass represents approximately 2-3 minutes of serial I/O that could be batched into a single reconcile_docs() call.

Pre-flight gate check not executed at every session start: the RETRO-022 workaround (apply_env_autofix) is called per-experiment, but the broader preflight (Exp 413 verdict check) is only validated at Gate 0 of each experiment script. There is no session-level gate that blocks the conductor from starting experiments if preflight is in an invalid state.
improvements_suggested: Fix CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE subprocess env inheritance at the conductor level (RETRO-022, systemic fix, 5-line change): In every conductor subprocess.run() call, pass env={**os.environ, 'CARNOT_FORCE_LIVE': '1'} explicitly. This is the correct systemic fix. The current apply_env_autofix() workaround (Exp 413) is a per-experiment band-aid — it works but requires every new experiment script to call it before any CUDA import. The conductor-level fix eliminates this per-script requirement and prevents future experiments from regressing if the call is omitted.

Implement conductor hard timeout as Experiment 1 of the next milestone (RETRO-003, carried 17+ milestones): 45 minutes per experiment, configurable per experiment type in the roadmap YAML. Emit a RETRO log entry and continue on timeout rather than hanging. PID 3509070 (144+ minutes, GPU 1 idle, GPU 0 at thermal limit) is the direct consequence of deferring this 17+ consecutive milestones. This MUST be Experiment 1, not a plan item that gets deprioritized.

Diagnose GPU 1 idle VRAM under PID 3509070 (RETRO-025): inspect whether the active experiment script calls DualGPURunner or explicitly allocates both GPUs. If it is a single-model experiment, GPU 1 should not be allocated at all. If it is a dual-model experiment, diagnose why GPU 1 compute is 0% — likely the second model did not load or the inference queue was not routed to GPU 1. Fix: add a DualGPURunner health check that logs VRAM and utilization on both GPUs 30 seconds after model load; fail fast if GPU 1 shows 0% utilization in a dual-model experiment.

Add GPU temperature guard in ExperimentTemplate.setup_gpu(): if any GPU exceeds 80C at the pre-warm health check, log a warning and throttle batch size by 25% to prevent reaching the 83-85C throttle region. GPU 0 is currently at 82C and has been there for 144+ minutes. The utilization drop (91% → 88%) between retro snapshots 23 minutes apart may already be thermal management.

Use targeted test reruns during debugging: when an experiment's test suite fails, run only the failing module's test file first (pytest tests/python/test_experiment_NNN*.py) before escalating to a full suite run. Full suite run only on the final pass before marking complete. This change alone would have saved approximately 24-32 minutes on Exp 308.

Add session-level preflight gate to conductor: at the start of each conductor session, run the Exp 413 preflight check. If honest_verdict is not in {gpu_confirmed_live, auto_fix_applied, gpu_detected_env_was_correct}, pause the conductor and prompt for human action rather than running a full milestone of blocked experiments.

Implement zombie detection in post-experiment teardown hook: run gpu_monitor --kill-zombies after each experiment completes, not just at session startup. PID 3509070 (1786MB on GPU 1, 0% util, 144+ minutes) would be detected and freed between experiments if teardown ran the monitor.

Batch doc reconciliation into a single pass: write a reconcile_docs() utility that updates changelog.md, status.md, conductor-log.md, metrics.md, traceability.md, and spec.md in one atomic pass rather than 4-6 sequential read-edit-write cycles. Reduces serial I/O overhead at experiment close.

Enforce checkpoint-resume in all new training experiments: conductor should verify that checkpoint_save() is called within the first epoch of any training loop before permitting a long-running CPU or GPU training job. Fail fast with a RETRO entry if the checkpoint infrastructure is missing.

Physical inspection of GPU cooling before next extended live run: GPU 0 reached 82C at 88% utilization after 144+ minutes. Given the 35-degree thermal delta between GPU 0 (82C active) and GPU 1 (47C idle), the chassis airflow is asymmetric. Clean both GPU heatsinks and verify fan curves are configured for sustained inference workloads (not gaming profiles). Do not start another 2-hour live run without confirming adequate cooling.

Write mid-milestone retro checkpoint: the retro for 2026.04.30 identified the RETRO-022 root cause only at milestone close; this retro captured a 144-minute runaway at the time of writing. A mid-milestone retro (after 50% of experiments) would surface thermal risk, zombie processes, and env propagation failures while there is still time to act within the same milestone.

savings_breakdown.note: 40% estimated savings is achievable in one milestone if the conductor-level RETRO-022 fix is applied and RETRO-003 is implemented as Experiment 1. The current PID 3509070 scenario (144+ minutes, GPU 1 idle, GPU 0 at thermal limit) exemplifies what 17+ milestones of deferring RETRO-003 produces. The savings estimate is conservative — fixing RETRO-003 and RETRO-025 together would recapture the wasted GPU 1 time in this experiment alone, which at 144 minutes represents over 10x the mean experiment duration.

what_went_well: First live GPU inference achieved in milestone 2026.04.31: Exp 413 apply_env_autofix() workaround enabled Exp 419 to pass Gate 0 and reach actual GPU inference. After eight consecutive milestones with zero live results, this is a meaningful milestone. GPU 0 is running at 88% utilization for 144+ minutes — the hardware is working.

RETRO-022 is now partially resolved: the apply_env_autofix() per-experiment workaround is implemented and tested (38 tests, 100% coverage). Exp 419 gates on it correctly. The path to live GPU results is clear.

CRANE extractor (Exp 418/419) reduces live GPU dependency for extraction: the CPU-only regex + deterministic-math extractor means FULL_STACK precision benchmarks can run without GPU for the extraction step, using GPU only for LLM inference.

GPU 1 partial zombie is VISIBLE and quantified: prior milestones had both GPUs idle (nothing to debug). This milestone has a live process holding GPU 1 memory at 0% utilization — a debuggable, concrete failure mode rather than a silent architectural gap.

Multi-snapshot GPU monitoring revealed thermal trend: comparing 16:00 UTC and 16:23 UTC snapshots shows GPU 0 steady at 82C while GPU 1 cooled from 51C to 47C and utilization on GPU 0 dropped from 91% to 88%. This is early thermal management evidence only visible through time-series snapshots.
what_went_poorly: RETRO-003 (conductor hard timeout) has now been carried 17+ milestones without implementation. PID 3509070 has run 144 minutes as of this retro — 3.2x the proposed 45-minute timeout. Every milestone plan includes it; it has never been Experiment 1; it has never shipped. This is structural deferral, not accidental oversight.

GPU 1 is allocated but idle in the live experiment: 1786MB held at 0% compute utilization for 144 minutes. If Exp 419 is a dual-model experiment, the second model (Qwen3.5-0.8B) is not inferring, which means precision benchmark results cover only one model variant despite the infrastructure claiming to support two.

GPU 0 temperature at 82C for 144+ minutes: this is within 1-3C of the thermal throttle threshold. The utilization dip (91% → 88% over 23 minutes) is a potential early sign of thermal management reducing GPU clock speed. Physical cooling was flagged in the 2026.04.30 retro and has not been actioned.

The systemic RETRO-022 fix (conductor subprocess.run env) was NOT applied despite being described as a 5-line change in the 2026.04.30 retro and again in the 2026.04.31 analysis. Instead, a per-experiment workaround was built. Systemic fixes should be preferred over per-script workarounds.
